sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of the title sheet of Asbury, a mill village on the Musconetcong River in Warren County, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. It shows Main running across the page from its junction with Washington Road and Bloomsbury Road, where it continues north as Broadway Road, south to the edge of sheet 2. The east side of Main (lots 201 to 220) is a single deep block bounded by Washington Road; most of it is open ground, with a few frame dwellings set well back from the street, barns, wagon houses, a fowl house, out houses and a small office at the corner of Washington Road (lot 406). The west side (lots 221 to 239) is a row of narrow lots with frame dwellings close to the street, a wheelwright shop drawn in green at lot 236, and sheds and wagon houses along the rear lot line; Bloomsbury Road bounds it on the west with lots 307 to 310. Nothing on the part is of brick or stone. A compass rose in block 3 and the scale of feet in block 4 are printed on the part. The lower centre of the page holds a separately boxed inset of the Bethlehem Township School on Ludlow Road, which is not part of this area. The rear of both blocks is marked no exposures. Lot numbers on Main are the arbitrary consecutive numbers the key describes, not house numbers.
notes: Washington Road is today Kitchen Road; Main is Old Main Street; Bloomsbury Road keeps its name.

Broadway Road (printed at the left edge) is the continuation of Main north of the junction, today Old Main Street; Anderson Road, which now leaves Old Main Street 45 m north of the junction, is not drawn.

Placed from the one detected junction (Main / Washington Road / Bloomsbury Road) and eight hand-picked parcel corners along Main; the sheet is drawn about 4 percent larger than its nominal 50 ft scale.

Title sheet with key, 50 ft to an inch, drawn with north to the left. Four parts: part 1 (main) Main Street from Washington Road and Bloomsbury Road south to sheet 2; part 2 the strip of Broadway Road (now Old Main Street) north of that junction, drawn above it; part 3 inset of Ludlow Road with the Asbury Roller Mills and mill pond (location unknown, no junction); part 4 inset of the Bethlehem Township School on Ludlow Road, 1 mile south of the post office. Washington Road = Kitchen Road, Broadway Road = Old Main Street (north of Kitchen Road).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Ludlow Road with the Asbury Roller Mills, mill pond and tail race (no street junction and no stated location; cannot be matched to modern roads or parcels with confidence; needs identification of the mill site (Ludlow Road, Musconetcong) and parcel-corner control).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Bethlehem Township School on Ludlow Road, located 1 mile south of the post office (single building, no street junction).

sheet-1-2.description: The upper half of the title sheet of Asbury, drawn above the main part at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left: Broadway Road running north from its junction with Washington Road and Bloomsbury Road on the right edge of the page, with the blocks on both sides. The east side (block 1, lots 101 to 122) is a row of long lots running back to vacant fields, with frame dwellings, small stables and outbuildings, and a blacksmith and wheelwright shop drawn in green at lot 118. The west side (block 2, lots 123 to 142) has frame dwellings near the street and a line of stables and wagon houses along a rear lot line, with barns, fowl houses and a wagon house towards Bloomsbury Road (lots 301 to 305). A boxed inset of Ludlow Road and the Asbury Roller Mills occupies the lower left of this half of the page and is not part of this area. The upper right holds the Sanborn Map Company cartouche (Asbury, Warren County, New Jersey, October 1909, population 500, scale 50 ft to an inch) and notes that water comes from wells and cisterns only, with no water works and no fire department; the key to the map is printed in block 2. The whole strip is frame buildings on open lots, the north end of the village.
notes: Broadway Road is today Old Main Street north of Kitchen Road (Washington Road); it becomes Asbury - Broadway Road further north.
Anderson Road, which now leaves Old Main Street about 45 m north of Kitchen Road and crosses the site of lot 118, is not drawn.

Placed from three points along the road (the Washington / Bloomsbury Road junction, hand-picked, and two parcel corners on the east side of Broadway Road at lots 106/107 and 108/109): a helmert fit, low confidence; drawn about 3 degrees from part 1, following the bend of the modern road.
Population 500; water from wells and cisterns only, no water works, no fire department, public lighting oil.

sheet-2-1.description: The centre of Asbury along Main, from the north edge of sheet 2 south to Water and the Musconetcong River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north roughly up. Church runs west from Main near the top. The west side of Main holds the village's commercial row: general stores, a barber, a confectionery, the post office in a stone building, a repository, marble works, a vacant store with a hall on the second floor and frame dwellings, several shown in brick. West of them on Church stand the Asbury Presbyterian Church (brick, with a tower and slated spire and an acetylene gas generator), a hitching shed and the public school. The east side has the American House hotel with a bar, a second hotel building, a restaurant, dwellings and the frame M.E. Church. At the south end Main widens and bends south-west towards the Asbury Graphite Mills on the river, drawn with grinding, bolting and storage buildings, a dynamo and turbine wheel, beside an iron bridge; a bake oven, storage building and a blacksmith shop stand by the mill pond east of Main, and Water runs east along its north side. A line marked as the cemetery boundary runs north-south east of Main. Two boxed insets on the sheet, Church further west and lots on Water a quarter mile south-east, are separate parts.
notes: Church is today School Street, Water is Maple Avenue and Main is Old Main Street.
Asbury Graphite Mills: run day and night, water power, own dynamo; a hydrant and 100 ft of hose fed from a pressure tank at the mill.

Placed from the detected Main / Church junction and five hand-picked parcel corners; the Main / Water junction is drawn as a wide irregular space and was not used. The sheet is drawn about 4 percent larger than its nominal 50 ft scale.

Church = School Street, Water = Maple Avenue.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Water Street lots 601-612 beside the cemetery, 1/4 mile south-east of the post office (no street junction; the lot pattern does not match modern parcels along Maple Avenue unambiguously; needs parcel-corner control once the lots are identified).

sheet-2-2.description: A small boxed inset at the top left of sheet 2 continuing Church westward beyond the left edge of the main part, at the same scale (50 feet to an inch) and orientation. It shows Church, 50 feet wide, with lots 15 to 20 on the north side and lots 33 to 38 on the south side, numbered on from the main part's lots 21 and 39. The north side has two frame dwellings, one of them with outbuildings; the south side has a frame dwelling and a small outbuilding at the west end and the parsonage, a frame building with rear additions, at lot 38 near the east end, close to the Presbyterian church drawn in the main part. The rest of the inset is open lots without buildings. A north arrow is printed in the inset.
notes: Church is today School Street; Mill Avenue, which now meets School Street in about the middle of this stretch, is not drawn.
No control of its own: placed by carrying four points from part 1, taking the inset as the direct continuation of part 1 to the west (lot numbers run on). Low confidence.
